newsitem.title: USA: House bans McVeigh burial with military honors.
newsitem.headline: House bans McVeigh burial with military honors.

text.p: The House voted unanimously on Monday to ban convicted terrorist Timothy McVeigh from burial with military honours in a national cemetery, echoing Senate action last week.

A federal jury in Denver sentenced McVeigh to death for the April 19, 1995, bombing of an Oklahoma federal building that killed 168 people. Veterans groups have been angered that McVeigh, as a decorated veteran of the Gulf War, could be buried in a national cemetery.

The lawmakers voted 416-0 to deny eligibility for burial with military honours to any service member convicted of a crime punishable by the death penalty and sentenced to either life imprisonment or death.
The Senate version would eliminate the possiblity of McVeigh's burial in a national cemetery by barring veteran benefits to anyone convicted of first-degree murder under federal law.
Benefits already are denied to those guilty of treason, sabotage, mutiny and other crimes.

Representative Spencer Bachus, an Alabama Republican said he sponsored the ban in response to a recent incident in his state in which a military funeral was given to a man executed in June for lynching a black teenager.

Henry Francis Hays, a member of the Ku Klux Klan was convicted of murdering the Mobile, Alabama teenager. Hays had served briefly in the Army in the early 1970s and was given a funeral with a 12-gun salute and a flag-draped coffin.
